newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NatCon says full yr difficult to forecast.
newsitem.headline: NatCon says full yr difficult to forecast.

text.p: Housing products and auto parts group National Consolidated Ltd said on Tuesday that its trading profit in the first half of calendar 1997 would be lower than expectations and the full year result was uncertain due to unpredictable market conditions.

The engineering company, which is 48.5 percent-owned by Malaysian Mining Bhd, said results in May and the performance in June indicated that profits would be below expectations. It did not detail the expected profit.
Sales were not benefitting from an improved housing market and were also affected by the weaker automotive sector.

"Whilst the company believes that the residential housing sector in Australia will grow in the second half, recent developments in the automotive industry indicate that some of the company's customers in that sector will be reducing their production schedules in the six months ending December," the company said.
"These unpredictable market conditions make it difficult for the company to comment on results for the year ending 31 December 1997."
The company achieved a pre-abnormal net profit of A$12.4 million in 1996 from A$16.7 million in 1995.
